Apply the following mathematical consult verbatim as the hard-subexperiment bridge; do not weaken it or treat the posterior-spread conclusion as proved:

The reviewer’s requested bridge is mathematically sound. It can be supplied exactly, without restricting Gamma, discarding assignment ancillaries, strengthening the model, or assuming the weighted-erasure posterior-spread assertion.

Lemma (hard-subexperiment embedding and interval reduction).
For v=(v_1,...,v_L) in {-1/2,1/2}^L, define the fixed block-homogeneous schedule m_v by Y_i^v(d)=v_l if d=a and Y_i^v(d)=0 if d != a, for i in B_l and d in E. Then m_v is in M_n(B), since the schedule is fixed and all its outcomes lie in [-1/2,1/2], and mu_l^v(a)=v_l, mu_l^v(b)=0, theta(m_v)=sum_l w_l v_l=T(v).

Under m_v, put K_l=A_l=1{Z_{B_l}=1}. Thus the K_l are independent Bernoulli(q_l) variables and Y_i^obs=K_l v_l for i in B_l. Consequently O_l=(K_l,K_l v_l) is measurable from the original data.

The remaining assignment information is retained as follows. Let nu_{l,1}=delta_1 and nu_{l,0}=Unif({0,1}^{B_l} minus {1}). Under balanced Bernoulli assignment, Law(Z | K=k)=product_l nu_{l,k_l}. In particular, when K_l=0, this conditional law retains both the all-control and every mixed assignment pattern, with their exact original probabilities; no ancillary-irrelevance claim is used.

Choose a Borel measure-preserving map beta:[0,1] -> [0,1]^{L+1}, beta(R)=(R_0,R_1,...,R_L), whose pushforward of Lebesgue measure is product Lebesgue measure. For each l, let F_l(k_l,R_l) sample nu_{l,k_l}, and define Z^*_{B_l}=F_l(K_l,R_l), Y_i^*=K_l V_l for i in B_l, and D^*=(Z^*,Y^*). For every measurable externally randomized original-data interval Gamma(D,R_0), define Lambda_Gamma(O,R)=Gamma(D^*(O,R_1,...,R_L),R_0).

This is measurable in (O,R). For every fixed v, Law(D^*,R_0 | V=v)=Law_{Z,R_0,m_v}(D,R_0). Hence the reduction preserves the entire randomized decision experiment, including pointwise coverage and expected length:
P_{K,R}{T(v) in Lambda_Gamma(O,R) | V=v}=P_{Z,R_0,m_v}{theta(m_v) in Gamma(D,R_0)},
E_{K,R}[len Lambda_Gamma(O,R) | V=v]=E_{Z,R_0,m_v}[len Gamma(D,R_0)].

Therefore, if Gamma is in C_alpha, Lambda_Gamma has coverage at least 1-alpha for every fixed v. Averaging under any tilted prior pi_t gives Q_t{T(V) in Lambda_Gamma(O,R)} >= 1-alpha. Moreover, for every t,
sup_{m in M_n(B)} E_{Z,R,m} len Gamma(D,R) >= sup_v E_{K,R}[len Lambda_Gamma | V=v] >= E_{Q_t} len Lambda_Gamma.
Taking the supremum over admissible t, applying the weighted-erasure spread result if and when it is proved, and then taking the infimum over Gamma in C_alpha yields the required minimax lower bound.
